subject: BridgePay: security gaps & retention review — post-call next steps
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Hayes <sarah.hayes@bridgepay.com>, Michael Tu <michael.tu@bridgepay.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-05T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: BridgePay: security gaps & retention review — post-call next steps

Hi Sarah / Michael —

Great to meet this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and suggested next steps so your security and procurement teams have a single source of truth. TL;DR: primary gaps you called out were audit-log retention, DPA wording around subprocessor disclosures, and the scope/details of recent penetration testing.

What we covered (high level):
- Pain: BridgePay needs 12+ month immutable audit logs (transaction/audit trail, admin actions), and a DPA that includes explicit audit rights and retention caps.
- Goal: evidence package (SOC 2 summary + pen-test high-level) + an initial retention matrix to map events -> retention policy by Sep 17 so procurement can set terms.
- Constraints: must support encrypted-at-rest key management (KMS/HSM), option for regional data residency, and limited exposure of raw logs to external vendors.

Agreed next steps I will drive:
1) Attach: redwood_soc2_summary_v3.pdf (short summary of scope and last audit date) and retention_matrix_bridgepay_draft.xlsx (initial mapping).
2) Karthik (cc) will add technical notes on audit log architecture, retention knobs, and pen-test vendor details.
3) Schedule an evidence-review call (30–45m) with your security ops + procurement — propose 2026-09-10 or 09-11.
4) Share a baseline DPA and confirm how you prefer to handle redlines (DocuSign or shared Google Doc).

Please confirm: preferred time for the evidence review, and whether your procurement team wants a draft DPA sent to procurement@bridgepay.com or to you first.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood_soc2_summary_v3.pdf], [Attachment: retention_matrix_bridgepay_draft.xlsx]

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | (415) 555-0189

On Sat, Sep 5, 2026 at 3:10 PM Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com> wrote:
> Great to meet this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and suggested next steps so your security and procurement teams have a single source of truth.

Thanks Monica — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we loop in procurement: 
- For "12+ month immutable audit logs" — do you support WORM storage for logs or are the logs logically immutable but stored in standard object storage with retention controls? We need to understand legal auditability.
- On pen test evidence: can you share the most recent external pen test scope and whether remediation items were tracked (and closed)?
- Procurement will also ask for a DPA redline process. Do you prefer DocuSign for an initial signature or to exchange a redline first?

I've attached our security questionnaire for context.

Attachments: [Attachment: bridgepay_security_questionnaire_v1.xlsx]

—Michael

Senior Security Engineer, BridgePay
michael.tu@bridgepay.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Michael Tu <michael.tu@bridgepay.com>, Sarah Hayes <sarah.hayes@bridgepay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-07T10:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BridgePay: security gaps & retention review — technical clarifications

Hi Michael / Sarah —

Thanks for the questions. A few technical clarifications to help procurement/security triage: 
- Logs & immutability: Redwood offers two retention options. By default logs are stored in encrypted object storage with retention policies and immutable buckets available (WORM) for customers who require legal immutability. We can export a time-series, per-request audit trail in CSV/NDJSON and store a signed digest for tamper-evidence.
- SOC 2 scope: the attached SOC2 summary covers the Redwood service control environment and hosted inference runtime (covering audit logging, change management, and incident response). The independent auditor and last report date are listed in the summary. Full report available under NDA.
- Pen test: we run annual external pentests plus quarterly internal red team exercises. The high-level vendor summary is attached as a stub; remediation items since the last external test were tracked in our internal tracker and most were closed within 30–60 days. We can provide the vendor report under an NDA and redact customer-sensitive details.
- DPA process: most customers prefer an initial redline exchange (tracked in Google Docs) followed by a DocuSign execution. Happy to follow whichever process procurement prefers.
- Regional residency: we can pin logs to region via Private deployment or our Dedicated offering; we'll include the deployment/cost tradeoffs in the retention matrix.

Proposed next step: evidence-review call — I can share a short runbook and we can bring our security ops engineer. Proposed slots: 2026-09-10 09:00–11:00 or 2026-09-11 14:00–16:00 PT. Calendar placeholder: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=bridgepay-evidence-review.

Attachments: [Attachment: pen_test_summary_stub.txt]

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com | (415) 555-0133

From: Sarah Hayes <sarah.hayes@bridgepay.com>

Subject: Re: BridgePay: security gaps & retention review — post-call next steps

Thanks all —

Appreciate the quick follow-up. Procurement and security want to run an evidence review on 2026-09-10 at 10:00 AM PT. Please send the DocuSign link for the baseline DPA (procurement prefers to see the executed template) and a short summary of items that will require procurement-level signoff (retention length, subprocessor list, audit rights). Also please include a rough run-rate estimate so I can flag budget to procurement (we're preliminarily evaluating Dedicated vs Hosted).

We received the SOC2 summary and questionnaire — we'll start with those and escalate for the full SOC2 report under NDA if necessary.

I'll add procurement@bridgepay.com to the calendar invite once you confirm the slot.

Thanks,
Sarah Hayes
